about.title: Covina Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product doesn't announce itself before it fails — a faulty appliance, a car part that gives out, a tool that malfunctions on the job. In Covina, where daily life moves along corridors like Badillo Street, Grand Avenue, and Citrus Avenue, defective products can turn an ordinary moment into a serious injury. California law recognizes this and generally applies strict liability to these cases, meaning an injured person typically doesn't have to prove a manufacturer was careless — only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. That standard can apply to the maker, the distributor, or the retailer who sold it. If you were hurt by something that didn't work the way it should have, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who handles these claims, free of charge, so you can focus on recovery while someone else sorts out the legal details.

whyChoose.title: Why Covina Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, the focus is usually on the product's condition and the harm it caused, not on proving carelessness.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, giving an attorney more avenues to pursue on your behalf.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving Evidence
items.desc: An attorney can advise you early on to keep the product itself intact, since it's often the most important piece of evidence in a defect claim.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often proceed under strict liability, which generally means you need to show the product was defective and that it caused your injury, rather than proving the manufacturer failed to act carefully. An independent attorney can review your specific situation to explain how this applies to you.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try to preserve it exactly as it was at the time of the injury, without repairing or discarding it. The product itself is often central evidence in these cases. Store it somewhere safe and photograph it if possible before speaking with an attorney.

items.question: Is this connected to Covina's traffic collision data?
items.answer: Not directly — product liability covers defective goods, not roadway collisions along corridors like Badillo Street or San Bernardino Road. However, some product defects, like a failed vehicle part, can factor into a crash, so it's worth mentioning the details of your incident when speaking with an attorney.
